nodes.What it is: Wheel speeds determine how the chassis moves. Differential drive cannot slide sideways, while mecanum rollers allow sideways motion under ideal contact assumptions.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Ideal no-slip models are a baseline, not a model of loose ground or roller friction. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulation or offline visualization is feasible with software skills; hardware transfer and compute are separate costs.

nodes.What it is: Static balance keeps the centre of mass over supporting feet. Dynamic balance also depends on momentum and contact forces; a support polygon alone cannot guarantee a moving robot will stay upright.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ZMP and contact feasibility remain useful abstractions but depend on contact and model assumptions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulation or offline visualization is feasible with software skills; hardware transfer and compute are separate costs.

nodes.What it is: A gait describes when each foot touches the ground and when it swings. Phase offsets and duty factors turn the same legs into walking, trotting or bounding patterns.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Contact timing and smooth transitions matter as much as a visually plausible repeated animation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulation or offline visualization is feasible with software skills; hardware transfer and compute are separate costs.

nodes.What it is: Simplified models replace many joints with a mass and a small number of contacts. The linear inverted pendulum approximates walking, while a spring-loaded inverted pendulum models bouncing and running.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: LIPM and SLIP expose useful structure but omit joint limits, impacts and much full-body dynamics. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulation or offline visualization is feasible with software skills; hardware transfer and compute are separate costs.

nodes.What it is: A central pattern generator is a coupled oscillator that produces rhythmic commands. Feedback can reset its phase when feet touch down, rather than replaying a fixed animation regardless of contact.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Biologically inspired rhythm generation is not by itself a guarantee of balance or terrain robustness. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulation or offline visualization is feasible with software skills; hardware transfer and compute are separate costs.

nodes.What it is: A biped repeatedly moves its support from one foot to the other. ZMP preview and capture-point ideas choose body motion and steps that help keep the robot from falling.
nodes.Prerequisites: Reduced-order models; feedback control; linear algebra
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Classical walking remains an interpretable baseline; uneven contacts and model errors challenge flat-ground assumptions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.Node: Model predictive control for legged robots
nodes.What it is: MPC repeatedly predicts a short future and optimizes contact forces or motions. Convex approximations can make this fast when contact timing is already chosen.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Convex MPC is not the same as solving arbitrary contact discovery; switched and nonlinear tools support richer models. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: MIT Biomimetics; ETH Robotic Systems Lab
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Whole-body control coordinates joints, body posture and contact forces together. It resolves competing tasks while respecting friction and actuator limits.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Task hierarchies and optimal-control solvers trade tracking quality against feasibility and computation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Reinforcement learning trains a policy by rewarding useful movement in simulation. Domain randomization varies friction, masses and delays so the policy is less tied to one simulated world.
nodes.Prerequisites: Python; neural networks; gait basics; feedback control
nodes.Frontier state 2026: legged_gym is a historical Isaac Gym baseline; current Isaac Lab and MuJoCo Playground offer newer workflows. Simulation success alone does not establish hardware transfer. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: ETH; NVIDIA Isaac Lab; Google DeepMind
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulation or offline visualization is feasible with software skills; hardware transfer and compute are separate costs.

nodes.What it is: Leg geometry and transmission choices change reach, force capability and impact behaviour. Proprioceptive actuation uses joint-side feedback to control interaction; this node focuses on mechanical trade-offs, not drive electronics.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Low inertia and backdrivability help contact control, but torque, heat and structural margins still constrain a design. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Perceptive walking uses terrain observations to adapt foot placement or body motion. Delayed or missing depth data can make an otherwise capable gait unsafe.
nodes.Prerequisites: Gaits; feedback; depth images; RL or MPC
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Parkour and recent predictive perception work connect terrain sensing to low-level control; benchmark terrain and sensor faults rather than claiming universal all-terrain ability. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Extreme Parkour authors; ETH; humanoid locomotion researchers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Recovery turns a fallen configuration into a stable standing pose. It needs contact-aware motions and a safe decision about when normal walking should resume.
nodes.Prerequisites: Contact dynamics; joint limits; RL basics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ANYmal research demonstrated learned recovery, but generalization to arbitrary falls, obstacles and damaged hardware is not established. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Rotors produce thrust and moments that control a flying body. Cascaded rate, attitude and position loops separate fast stabilization from slower movement commands.
nodes.Prerequisites: Rigid-body rotations; PID; forces and torque
nodes.Frontier state 2026: PX4 documents controller architecture; this is flight stabilization, not aerial mapping or path planning. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: A small simulation or offline visualization is feasible with software skills; hardware transfer and compute are separate costs.

nodes.What it is: Wheel-legged robots can roll for efficiency and step when terrain demands it. The controller must coordinate rolling constraints, contact forces and transitions between modes.
nodes.Prerequisites: Wheeled kinematics; legged contact dynamics; MPC or RL
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Recent hybrid work couples rolling, stepping and body interaction; many papers use platform-specific assets rather than a universal controller. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Wheel-legged research teams in the opened arXiv results
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Retargeting converts human motion to a robot with different joints and proportions. A tracking policy then learns physically possible whole-body movement rather than directly replaying impossible joint angles.
nodes.Prerequisites: Robot kinematics; motion data; RL; contact dynamics
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DeepMimic is foundational; OmniH2O and RSS 2025 ASAP address robot motion tracking and deployment mismatch. Human video does not automatically yield safe robot motions. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: DeepMimic authors; CMU; UC San Diego; collaborating humanoid teams
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Agile locomotion includes rapid jumps, dynamic obstacle crossing and fast contact changes. It combines precise timing, perception and control rather than just increasing walking speed.
nodes.Prerequisites: Perceptive walking; RL; contact dynamics; recovery
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Extreme Parkour reports impressive bounded course performance; safe extrapolation beyond training obstacles remains an open question. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Loco-manipulation coordinates balance and stepping while the robot interacts with an object. The focus here is how object forces and carried mass affect locomotion, not general grasp perception.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: OmniH2O and recent visual humanoid work connect whole-body skills and interaction, but long-horizon robustness needs careful evaluation. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: OmniH2O authors; recent humanoid research teams
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

nodes.What it is: Cross-embodiment learning aims to reuse movement knowledge across bodies with different proportions or joints. A shared policy still needs a representation of each robot and careful testing on unseen bodies.
nodes.Prerequisites: RL locomotion; robot morphology; motion representations
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Recent generalist and rapid-adaptation preprints propose broader reuse; transfer across many real bodies remains a research question, not a turnkey low-cost platform. Snapshot of opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Generalist humanoid and quadruped adaptation researchers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Simulation avoids procurement, but contact dynamics, tuning and asset compatibility need substantial study.

top3.justification: Very accessible phase animation and visible gait changes, a simulation-first route to Bittle/Pupper communities, and no initial hardware purchase. Physical demos still need a quote and safety review.
Strong software/AI fit and striking learned walking videos using public frameworks. Simulation avoids robot purchase, but GPU time and transfer risk reduce the apparent low-cost advantage.

Human-to-humanoid motion makes compelling videos and connects to active humanoid research. Start with offline retargeting, not a humanoid purchase; physically robust tracking is harder than skeleton animation.
